item.title: Central North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ACPN50 PHFO 241149
TWOCP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 AM HST Mon Aug 24 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lala, located several hundred miles north of Pearl and Hermes
Atoll, on Tropical Depression Moke, located several hundred miles
south of Honolulu, Hawaii, and on Tropical Storm Iselle, located
several hundred miles southwest of the southern tip of the Baja
California Peninsula.

Western East Pacific:
A broad area of low pressure is forecast to form well to the
east-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands during the middle part of the
week. Some slow development of this system is possible later this
week while it moves northeastward or northward across the western
portion of the East Pacific.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

&&

Public Advisories on Tropical Storm Iselle are issued under WMO
header WTPZ34 NHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP4.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Iselle are issued under WMO
header WTPZ24 and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP4.

...LALA HOLDING STEADY MOVING NORTHWESTWARD...

LOCATION...33.4N 175.3W

PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 320 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...988 MB...29.18 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 AM HST (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Lala was
located near latitude 33.4 North, longitude 175.3 West. Lala is
moving toward the northwest near 5 mph (7 km/h). A slow
northwestward motion is forecast during the next few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 65 mph (100 km/h) with higher
gusts. Gradual weakening is forecast during the next several days.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 175 miles (280 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 988 mb (29.18 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.

-------------

item.title: Tropical Storm Lala Forecast Discussion Number 49
item.description:
Issued at 500 AM HST Mon Aug 24 2026 
000
WTPA42 PHFO 241436
TCDCP2
 
Tropical Storm Lala Discussion Number  49
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM HST Mon Aug 24 2026
 
Lala has remained steady state with a curved band that wraps about
three-quarters of the way around the center. Convection persists
even as the storm traverses cooler sea surface temperatures.
Satellite intensity estimates from HFO, JTWC, and UW-CIMSS range
from 45 to 62 kt. Scatterometer data that arrived shortly after the
previous advisory shows a peak wind of 44 kt, and was used to adjust
the wind radii on the western side of the system. Given the
steady-state satellite appearance and a blend of the estimates and
scatterometer data, the initial intensity is held at 55 kt.
 
The storm is moving slowly northwestward (320/4 kt). A slow and 
generally northwestward motion is expected to continue for the next 
several days while the system is steered by a ridge to the 
northeast. The latest NHC forecast track shows Lala crossing the 
International Date Line just beyond 72 h. The official track 
forecast was nudged slightly to the left in the short term and lies 
close to the latest HCCA consensus aid.
 
Lala has continued to produce convection over cool sea surface
temperatures within a low wind shear environment. As SSTs decrease
further along the forecast track, the cyclone will increasingly
struggle to sustain this convective activity. Thus, a slow weakening
trend is forecast to continue during the next few days. The official
intensity forecast lies near the middle of the guidance envelope and
is similar to the previous prediction. Simulated infrared satellite
imagery from the global models suggests Lala will fail to maintain
organized deep convection between days 3 and 4, and the system is
forecast to become a post-tropical cyclone by 96 h.

item.description:
Issued at 500 AM HST Mon Aug 24 2026 
000
WTPA33 PHFO 241435
TCPCP3
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Depression Moke Advisory Number  17
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP022026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM HST Mon Aug 24 2026
 
...FLASH FLOOD THREAT CONTINUES FOR PORTIONS OF THE BIG ISLAND OF 
HAWAII...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 AM HST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...15.5N 160.2W
ABOUT 445 MI...715 KM SW OF HILO HAWAII
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 280 DEGREES AT 14 MPH...22 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1004 MB...29.65 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 AM HST (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression Moke was
located near latitude 15.5 North, longitude 160.2 West. The
depression is moving toward the west near 14 mph (22 km/h). and this
motion is expected to continue for the next day or two, taking the 
system farther away from the Hawaiian Islands.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts.
Weakening is expected, and Moke is forecast to degenerate to a
remnant low pressure area late today and dissipate on Tuesday.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1004 mb (29.65 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Tropical Depression Moke can be found in the
Tropical Cyclone Discussion under AWIPS header HFOTCDCP3 and WMO
header WTPA43 PHFO.
 
RAINFALL: Tropical Depression Moke is expected to produce additional 
rainfall amounts of 2 to 4 inches through Monday across the Big 
Island and an additional 1 to 3 inches on eastern Maui. This 
rainfall may produce areas of flash flooding for the windward and 
southeast Big Island, especially in steep terrain and over areas 
that were affected recently by Lala. Flood prone and low lying 
locations, as well as urban areas may also see instances of flash 
flooding. 
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Moke,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_cp3.shtml?rainqpf.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 AM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Blake

item.title: Tropical Depression Moke Forecast Discussion Number 17
item.description:
Issued at 500 AM HST Mon Aug 24 2026 
016 
WTPA43 PHFO 241436
TCDCP3
 
Tropical Depression Moke Discussion Number  17
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP022026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM HST Mon Aug 24 2026

Moke continues to be in a disorganized state, with only sporadic 
bursts of convection in the northern semicircle.  A recent OSCAT 
pass showed maximum winds of about 30 kt in a small area on the 
northern side of the circulation, so the initial intensity will 
remain 30 kt on this advisory.  The scatterometer pass also showed 
that the circulation was losing definition and becoming somewhat 
elongated.  Given this structure and the persistent shear plus 
dry environment, Moke is not likely to hold onto tropical-cyclone 
status for much longer.  Thus the new forecast shows that Moke will 
dissipate later today, which is consistent with the latest model 
guidance.  

The depression continues moving slightly north of due west at about 
12 kt.  A strong low- to mid-level ridge should hold firm north of 
Moke until the cyclone dissipates.  The new forecast is similar to 
the last forecast and is on the southern side of the guidance.   
Even though Moke is well south of the Hawaiian Islands, periods of 
heavy rain causing flash flooding are possible across portions of 
the Big Island today.
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Rain bands associated with Tropical Depression Moke will continue 
over the Hawaiian Islands through Monday. This rainfall may produce 
areas of flash flooding for the windward and southeast Big Island, 
especially in steep terrain and over areas that were affected 
recently by Lala. Flood prone and low lying locations, as well as 
urban areas, may also see instances of flash flooding.
